prompt:
A flat, matte design sketch of a desktop website homepage, landscape 16:9, shown straight on with no perspective, no device frame, no browser chrome, no drop shadows, no gloss, no photorealism. Deliberately unfinished, like a designer's layout study rendered in flat color blocks.

Palette, used exactly: warm aged-paper off-white background (#F7F3ED), dark warm ink (#2A231C), one muted slate blue accent (#365778). No other colors. A faint regular dot grid over the paper background.

The page is built entirely from large typography. There are no photographs, no screenshots, no bordered panels, and no cards anywhere.

Composition, top to bottom:

A thin quiet header strip across the very top with the word Narraitor small on the left.

Below it, a serif headline across the left half reading exactly: Play a story in any world you can imagine

Directly beneath it, one solid slate-blue rectangular button. Keep this compact.

Then the body of the page, which fills the remaining three quarters: roughly eight entries stacked vertically, each separated from the next by a thin full-width hairline rule.

Each entry has this anatomy: a very small greeked tag in the left margin, then to its right one or two lines of LARGE bold greeked text, rendered as thick heavy horizontal bars. These bars must be visibly much larger and heavier than ordinary body text, at roughly the weight and scale of a subheading.

Vary the entries so the page has rhythm: some entries are a single long bar running most of the width, some are two shorter stacked bars, some are one short punchy bar taking only a third of the width. The variation in length and stacking is important. Two or three of the entries have one segment of their bar rendered in slate blue instead of dark ink.

The whole effect should be a dense vertical stack of big bold statements in different shapes, like a list of opening sentences set at poster scale, with small quiet labels beside each.

A thin footer strip at the very bottom with three small greeked links.

The only legible text anywhere is the word Narraitor and the headline. Every other text region is greeked: indistinct horizontal bars standing in for words, not real letters. Do not render invented prices, dates, statistics, logos, faces, or photographs.

The overall feeling is a boldly typeset broadside or a table of contents printed at unusual scale: quiet paper, loud type.
